noun

### state noun (CONDITION)

Add to word list Add to word list

B2 [\[ C \]](https://dictionary.cambridge.org/help/codes.html)

a [condition](https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/condition "condition") or way of being that [exists](https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/exist "exists") at a [particular](https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/particular "particular") [time](https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/time "time"):

a state of The [building](https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/building "building") was in a state of [disrepair](https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/disrepair "disrepair").

state of mind She was [found](https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/found "found") [wandering](https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/wander "wandering") in a [confused](https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/confused "confused") state of [mind](https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/mind "mind").

Give me the [keys](https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/key "keys") - you're not in a state to [drive](https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/drive "drive").

in a state of shock After the [accident](https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/accident "accident") I was in a state of [shock](https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/shock "shock").

state of affairs I came [home](https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/home "home") to an [unhappy](https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/unhappy "unhappy") state of [affairs](https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/affair "affairs") (= [situation](https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/situation "situation")).

The [kitchen](https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/kitchen "kitchen") was in [its](https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/its "its") [original](https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/original "original") state, with a 1920s [sink](https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/sink "sink") and [stove](https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/stove "stove").

 **the state of play** UK

the [present](https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/present "present") [situation](https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/situation "situation"):

the state of play in The [article](https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/article "article") [provides](https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/provide "provides") a [useful](https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/useful "useful") [summary](https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/summary "summary") of the [current](https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/current "current") state of [play](https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/play "play") in the [negotiations](https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/negotiation "negotiations").

[See more](https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/state-of-play "meaning of the state of play")

*   The [old](https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/old "old") [railway](https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/railway "railway") [cottages](https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/cottage "cottages") were in a state of [dereliction](https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/dereliction "dereliction").
*   The [whole](https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/whole "whole") [office](https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/office "office") was in a state of [disorder](https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/disorder "disorder").
*   Over the [years](https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/year "years") the [church](https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/church "church") has [fallen](https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/fallen "fallen") into a state of [neglect](https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/neglect "neglect").
*   I was in a state of [shock](https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/shock "shock") for about two [weeks](https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/week "weeks") after the [accident](https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/accident "accident").
